extraction.name: Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI) Benchmark
extraction.description: A multimodal benchmark comprising 20,000 self-contradictory instruction conflicts, evenly distributed between language-language (L-L) and vision-language (V-L) paradigms, designed to evaluate the capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) in recognizing conflicting commands. It encompasses 8 tasks: RuleConflict, AttributeConflict, ExclusionConflict, ForbbidenConflict, OCRConflict, FigureConflict, GeometricConflict, and SemanticConflict. The dataset is constructed using an automatic dataset creation framework called AutoCreate, and is provided in three splits: SCI-Core (1%), SCI-Base (10%), and SCI-All (100%).
extraction.creator: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, Dequan Wang (Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Fudan University, Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory)
extraction.citeAs: Gao, J., Gan, L., Li, Y., Ye, Y., & Wang, D. (2024). Dissecting Dissonance: Benchmarking Large Multimodal Models Against Self-Contradictory Instructions. arXiv:2408.01091v2 [cs.AI].
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is constructed using AutoCreate, a novel automatic dataset creation framework that leverages programs and large language models (LLMs). AutoCreate starts from a small batch of manually input seeds and automatically generates large quantities of high-quality, diverse data through iterative cycles. Each cycle includes a Language Loop and a Visual Loop, each processed by a Generator, Decorator, and Cleaner. Both human experts and LLMs are involved in double-checking the quality of the generated dataset. For SemanticConflict, the ImageNet dataset is used as an external data source.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Software Collection, Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Seeds manually input by researchers; ImageNet dataset (imagenet-1k validation set) used for SemanticConflict; LLM-generated texts for language-language conflicts; programmatically generated images for vision-language conflicts.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For FigureConflict, the data dictionary is tampered with by changing the largest value to the smallest value before plotting the chart. For GeometricConflict, attribute descriptions are exchanged to introduce confusion. For SemanticConflict, the correct class label in questions is substituted with a similar but different object. For OCRConflict, images are generated with varying font, size, and color to augment diversity.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A Cleaner module removes data that does not meet quality standards. Human experts rigorously check the quality of the AutoCreate-generated dataset. Three levels of splits are manually selected: SCI-Core (1%), SCI-Base (10%), and SCI-All (100%). ExclusionConflict, ForbbidenConflict, and OCRConflict require extra effort to guarantee diversity when used in SCI-Core. For ForbbidenConflict, an LLM agent judges whether the answers to generated questions are unique.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Evaluation (annotation of whether a reply successfully identifies the conflict) is first conducted by human experts. LLMs (specifically GPT-4) are also used as evaluation agents. A uniform prompt for all tasks is designed to prompt LLMs as evaluation agents. Spearman correlation coefficient and concordance rate are calculated to measure consistency between human and LLM evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: GPT-4 demonstrates close alignment to human evaluative standards. Spearman correlation coefficients between GPT-4 and human experts are: GPT-4V replies: 0.881 (94% concordance), LLaVA-1.5 replies: 0.999 (99% concordance), Gemini replies: 0.854 (97% concordance). ChatGLM evaluation results exhibit slight numerical discrepancy compared to ChatGPT but demonstrate similar trends.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors state that more modalities will be included in the SCI benchmark based on the AutoCreate framework in future work. No explicit versioning or deprecation policy is described.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The SCI benchmark provides researchers and practitioners with a standardized platform to assess and enhance LMMs' ability to navigate conflicting instructions, advancing human-computer interaction and communication technologies. The AutoCreate framework facilitates the creation of diverse instruction datasets, promoting inclusivity in AI research. The CaP approach integrates external cognition into multimodal models, enhancing context-aware understanding. By improving dissonance detection, the approach boosts LMM performance and fosters trust and reliability in AI systems, essential for societal integration. The benchmark addresses challenges particularly relevant to language beginners and vulnerable populations who may not realize potential multimodal conflicts.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark only includes language-language and vision-language paradigms; more modalities are not yet included. No fine-grained control is introduced to determine the conflict degree. No detailed study is provided on the attention mechanism of large multimodal models when confronted with conflict instructions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluation of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) on their ability to detect self-contradictory instructions. The dataset supports qualitative evaluation at three levels of difficulty (SCI-Core, SCI-Base, SCI-All). It can be used to test prompting approaches such as few-shot, chain-of-thought, self-consistency, and Cognitive Awakening Prompting (CaP). Not recommended for use as training data for instruction-following without careful consideration of conflict-inducing properties.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 (used as evaluation agent for determining whether replies identify conflicts); ChatGPT (used as evaluation agent for L-L tasks); ChatGLM (used as evaluation agent for L-L tasks)
